answer: A deposit-and-history gate resists sybil attacks: each agent identity must lock a refundable deposit and earn weight through a record of verifiable useful work. New identities start near zero, so one operator cloning an identity into a mere echo gains no extra influence; each fake needs its own deposit and work history, so attacker cost scales linearly with fleet size. Like a falcon that must keep hunting, a reputation signal that decays without continued honest work, plus slashing deposits for coordinated fraud, leaves fakes stranded on a dune of sunk costs while honest agents pay once.
